## 1. Historical Background

### Timeline

| Year | Contributor | Contribution |
|------|-------------|--------------|
| 1960s | Control theorists | Foundational gradient-based optimization concepts |
| 1974 | Paul Werbos | PhD thesis: First description of backpropagation for neural networks |
| 1986 | Rumelhart, Hinton, Williams | Popularized backpropagation in Nature paper |
| 1989 | Yann LeCun | Applied backpropagation to CNNs for handwritten digit recognition |
| 1998 | LeCun et al. | LeNet-5 demonstrated practical success |
| 2012 | AlexNet (Krizhevsky et al.) | Revived deep learning; ImageNet breakthrough |
| 2015+ | Various | Adam, batch normalization, residual connections mature |

### Why It Took So Long

- **Computational cost**: Early computers couldn't handle the matrix multiplications
- **Data scarcity**: Large networks need large datasets
- **Initialization problems**: Poor initialization caused vanishing gradients
- **Paradigm shift**: Connectionist approach was controversial vs. symbolic AI

- $W_2 \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{out} \times d_{hidden}}$: second layer weights
- $b_2 \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{out}}$: second layer bias
- $\sigma$: element-wise activation function (e.g., sigmoid, ReLU)
- $\mathcal{L}$: loss function
